name: yxml
workload: Parsing two real-world XML dumps end-to-end (162 MiB Wikipedia XML dump and 94 MiB Discogs XML dump), measuring wall-clock parse time; also benchmarked against Expat and Mini-XML (mxml) on the same files.
claimed_speedup: ~2.2-2.4x faster than libxml2 (1.15s vs 2.53s on the Wikipedia dump, 0.74s vs 1.75s on the Discogs dump, both gcc 4.8.1 -O2) (derived from page data); ~1.3-1.5x faster than Expat (1.15s vs 1.47s, 0.74s vs 1.09s) on the same runs
tradeoffs: Minimal 3-function pull-style/streaming API, no malloc(), only 6 KiB object code; non-validating beyond well-formedness checks; no DTD, namespaces, XSLT, or XPath support; cannot parse non-ASCII-compatible encodings directly.
caveats: Benchmark dates to ~2013-2014 on a 2008-era CPU (Core Duo E8400); not compared against pugixml or RapidXML (only Expat, libxml2, Mini-XML); it is the author's own personal project page/blog, not independently reproduced; repo (self-hosted cgit, occasionally mirrored unofficially on GitHub) has had no commits since 2020-11-08.
found_via: Blogs / talks (personal blog): HN Algolia search 'fast XML parser' surfaced 'Show HN: A 6KB, fast and mostly-correct XML parser in C' -> http://dev.yorhel.nl/yxml, opened directly for the benchmark table and repo tree
